intro_en: In this lesson you learn to describe a noun with a whole sentence. For example: "the bus that goes to Kyoto", "the food Mother made", "the person wearing glasses". Tamil puts a describing verb form before the noun, like "போகும்" (that goes) or "செய்த" (that was made). Japanese does the same. It puts a plain-form verb (the short form) right before the noun. This lesson also has words for clothes and colours. You will learn verbs for wearing, and words for looking for a house.

g22-1.explanation_en: In Tamil, a describing verb form comes before the noun. For example, "போகும்" (that goes) or "வாங்கிய" (that was bought). You say "கியோட்டோவுக்குப் போகும் பஸ்" (the bus that goes to Kyoto). You say "நேற்று வாங்கிய காலணி" (the shoes I bought yesterday). Japanese uses the same order. Write the whole sentence in the plain form (普通形, the short form). Then put the noun after it: 京都へ行くバス、昨日買った靴. English needs "which" or "that", but Japanese doesn’t. Just like Tamil, the noun comes last. You can use all four forms: 行く (that goes)、行かない (that doesn’t go)、行った (that went)、行かなかった (that didn’t go). For "is doing now" or "is in a state", use 〜ている + noun: 眼鏡を掛けている人. A noun described like this works like any other noun. It can take は、が、を、に and so on.
g22-1.tamil_parallel_en: "கியோட்டோவுக்குப் போகும் பஸ்" (the bus that goes to Kyoto) = 京都へ行くバス ； "நேற்று வாங்கிய காலணி" (the shoes bought yesterday) = 昨日買った靴. Both languages put the describing verb right before the noun. Nothing like "which" comes in between.
g22-1.formation_en: Verb plain form (行く / 行かない / 行った / 行かなかった / 〜ている) + noun
g22-1.pitfalls_en: Putting the ます-form before a noun is wrong: ×行きますバス → ○行くバス. To describe a state like "wearing", you need the 〜ている form: 掛けている人. 掛ける人 changes the meaning. It means "a person who is going to put on glasses".

g22-2.explanation_en: In Lesson 8 you learned how adjectives (describing words) go before a noun. い-adjectives come right before the noun: 大きい帽子. な-adjectives take な: 静かな部屋. To join two adjectives, use the 〜くて / 〜で form from Lesson 16: 白くて大きな帽子 (a big white hat), 広くて明るい部屋. When you speak, you can also just put them side by side: 赤い長いスカート. This lesson has 大きな and 小さな. Like な-adjectives, they only come before a noun. You can say 大きいです, but you cannot end a sentence with 大きなです. You can also use a verb part and an adjective together: 駅に近い静かな部屋 (a quiet room near the station). It is just like Tamil: "வெள்ளையான பெரிய தொப்பி" (a white, big hat).
g22-2.tamil_parallel_en: "வெள்ளையான பெரிய தொப்பி" (a white big hat) = 白くて大きな帽子 ； "விசாலமான வெளிச்சமான அறை" (a spacious bright room) = 広くて明るい部屋. Like Tamil, Japanese just lines up the describing words before the noun.
g22-2.formation_en: い-adjective くて + adjective + noun ； な-adjective で + adjective + noun ； adjective + adjective + noun ； 大きな / 小さな + noun
g22-2.pitfalls_en: Forgetting な after a な-adjective is a common mistake: ×静か部屋 → ○静かな部屋. Don’t put 大きな at the end of a sentence like 大きい: ×この犬は大きなです → ○大きいです.

g22-3.explanation_en: This is a special use of g22-1. Some nouns are 時間 (time), 約束 (promise, plan to meet) and 用事 (an errand, something you have to do). Before them, put a dictionary-form verb that says "to do what". For example: 服を買う時間 (time to buy clothes), 映画を見る約束 (a promise to see a movie), 銀行へ行く用事 (an errand to go to the bank). It matches Tamil phrases like "வாங்க நேரம் இல்லை" (no time to buy). Another one is "பார்க்க வாக்கு கொடுத்தேன்" (I promised to see). After these, you usually say があります or がありません. You can also say 約束をします (I make a promise). Here you always use the dictionary form (the form for now or later). Don’t use the past form.
g22-3.tamil_parallel_en: "உடை வாங்க நேரம் இல்லை" (no time to buy clothes) = 服を買う時間がありません ； "வங்கிக்குப் போக வேலை இருக்கிறது" (I have an errand to go to the bank) = 銀行へ行く用事があります. The Tamil "to" form ("வாங்க", "போக") comes before the noun. It matches the Japanese dictionary form.
g22-3.formation_en: Verb dictionary form + 時間 / 約束 / 用事 + が あります / ありません
g22-3.pitfalls_en: To ask "do you have time?", say 時間がありますか. Don’t use 時間を because of Tamil "நேரத்தை". The ます-form doesn’t come before 時間: ×買います時間 → ○買う時間.

g22-4.explanation_en: Here we compare two forms that sound alike. 〜ましょうか from Lesson 14 offers help. It means "shall I do it?": 持ちましょうか (shall I carry it?). 〜ましょう from Lesson 6 asks someone to do something with you. It means "let’s do it": 食べましょう (let’s eat). Tamil has the same difference. "தூக்கட்டுமா?" (shall I carry?) is about "I", plus "ஆ" to ask. "சாப்பிடுவோம்" (let’s eat) is about "we". To answer ましょうか, you can say お願いします (yes please). Or you can say いいえ、結構です (no, thank you). To answer ましょう, you can agree with ええ、〜ましょう or いいですね. ましょうか can also be an invitation: "shall we do it?". But for N5, the "offer help" meaning is the important one.
g22-4.tamil_parallel_en: "நான் தூக்கட்டுமா?" (shall I carry it?) = 持ちましょうか ； "(நாம்) சாப்பிடுவோம்" (let’s eat) = 食べましょう. Tamil uses different endings. "-அட்டுமா" is for an offer, and "-வோம்" is for "let’s". Japanese uses ましょうか and ましょう.
g22-4.formation_en: Verb ます-stem (the part before ます) + ましょうか (shall I do it?) ； Verb ます-stem + ましょう (let’s do it)
g22-4.pitfalls_en: When you offer help, don’t forget か. Without か, the meaning changes to "let’s carry it (together)": 持ちましょう ≠ 持ちましょうか. When you answer ましょうか, お願いします is more polite than just はい.

g22-5.explanation_en: Sometimes the describing part has its own doer (the person who does the action). Mark that doer with が, not は. For example: 母が作った料理 (the food Mother made), 友達が住んでいる町 (the town where my friend lives). Why? は marks the topic of the whole sentence (what you are talking about). The doer inside the small describing part takes が. Full sentence: 母は料理を作りました. Describing a noun: 母が作った料理. In Tamil "அம்மா செய்த சாப்பாடு" (the food Mother made), "அம்மா" does not change. But in Japanese, it changes to が. Watch for this. The same rule works inside words like 好きな and 欲しい: 私が好きな色 (the colour I like). In short describing parts, の can also replace が (母の作った料理). But for N5, が is enough.
g22-5.tamil_parallel_en: "அம்மா செய்த சாப்பாடு" (the food Mother made) = 母が作った料理 (the doer inside the describing part takes が) ； "அம்மா சாப்பாடு செய்தார்" (Mother made food) = 母は料理を作りました (the topic takes は). In Tamil, "அம்மா" looks the same in both. But Japanese changes は to が.
g22-5.formation_en: Doer が + verb (plain form) + noun ； doer が + adjective + noun
g22-5.pitfalls_en: Using は inside the describing part is a very common mistake: ×母は作った料理 → ○母が作った料理. Look at "this is the food Mother made". The topic of the whole sentence is これは. Inside the describing part, it is 母が.

g22-6.explanation_en: This form tells what something is by an action that already happened. For example: "this is the sweater my sister knitted". Or: "that is the coat I bought last year". Put the た-form from Lesson 19 before the noun: 作った、買った、撮った、もらった. Mark the person who did it with が. It matches the Tamil past describing forms exactly: "செய்த" (that was made), "வாங்கிய" (that was bought). You often see this pattern: これ / それ / あれ + は + [describing part] + noun + です. To ask a question, say 誰が作ったNですか. It is about the past, so don’t use 作ります or 作る. The た shows the action is finished.
g22-6.tamil_parallel_en: "இது அக்கா பின்னிய ஸ்வெட்டர்" (this is the sweater my older sister knitted) = これは姉が作ったセーターです. The Tamil past forms "பின்னிய" / "செய்த" match the た-form 作った.
g22-6.formation_en: これ / それ / あれ は + person が + verb た-form + noun です
g22-6.pitfalls_en: Don’t use ました instead of the た-form: ×姉が作りましたセーター → ○姉が作ったセーター. To ask "who made it?", also use 誰が (with が), not 誰は.

items.L22-q01: 上着 = うわぎ (மேலங்கி, jacket). Here 上 is read うわ, not うえ. 着 is read ぎ, with the two dots (゛). うわき, without the dots, is the trap.
items.L22-q02: 靴 = くつ (காலணி, shoes). くち is 口 (mouth). くず is a different word. ぐつ, with the dots, is never used on its own.
items.L22-q03: 眼鏡 = めがね (மூக்குக் கண்ணாடி, glasses). This is a special reading. がんきょう reads each kanji the Chinese way. But that reading is not used for this word. めかね has lost the dots (が).
items.L22-q04: ぼうし = 帽子 (தொப்பி, hat). 帽 must have 巾 (cloth) on its left side. 冒 does not have it, so it is a fake. The second kanji is 子 (こ/し), not 字 (じ).
items.L22-q05: ひろい = 広い (விசாலமான, spacious). 太い (ふとい, thick) looks similar, but it is a different adjective. 庭 (にわ, garden) and 店 (みせ, shop) are nouns. Adding い to them makes no word at all.
items.L22-q06: For glasses, use 掛けます (கண்ணாடி அணிய, put on glasses). 着る is for clothes on the top half of the body. かぶる is for the head. はく is for clothes on the bottom half and for shoes. In Japanese, the verb for "wear" changes with the part of the body.
items.L22-q07: A hat goes on the head, so use かぶります (தலையில் அணிய, put on the head). 着ます is only for clothes on the top half of the body, like shirts and coats.
items.L22-q08: Skirts, trousers, shoes and socks are worn below the waist. All of them take はきます (கீழ் உடை அணிய, put on lower-body clothes). 着て is only for clothes on the top half. Be careful. Tamil uses "அணிய" (wear) for everything.
items.L22-q09: "There is only a bed", so the room is 狭い (குறுகலானது, small/narrow). 広い and 大きい mean the opposite. 明るい (bright) doesn’t tell the size of a place.
items.L22-q10: 何色 (なにいろ) = (எந்த நிறம், what colour). 黒 and 青 are real colours. They don’t make a question with 何.
items.L22-q11: 着て is for wearing on the top half of the body. So the answer is 背広 (சூட், suit). 靴, 靴下 and ズボン take はきます, not 着ます.
items.L22-q12: 狭い (குறுகலான, small) = 大きくない (not big). 広い means the exact opposite.
items.L22-q13: 母が作ったセーター comes from the sentence 母はセーターを作りました (அம்மா ஸ்வெட்டர் செய்தார், Mother made the sweater). Here the sentence describes the noun. "Bought" and "received" are different actions.
items.L22-q14: "No time to buy" means I won’t buy today (買いません, வாங்க மாட்டேன்). 買いたいです (I want to buy) is a wish. It is not about time.
items.L22-q15: A verb that describes a noun comes right before it, in the plain form (the short form): 行くバス (போகும் பஸ், the bus that goes). 行きますバス is wrong. Adding の, as in 行くの, is also wrong. Don’t translate Tamil "போகிற" with の.
items.L22-q16: Use 〜ている for the state of "wearing". Before a noun, use the plain form (short form) 掛けている (அணிந்திருக்கும், who is wearing). 掛けています ends a sentence. It doesn’t come before a noun.
items.L22-q17: The doer inside a describing part takes が: 母が作った料理. Using は is a common mistake. は is only for the topic of the whole sentence, これは.
items.L22-q18: 昨日 (yesterday) shows it is past. Before a noun, you need the short past form 買った (வாங்கிய, that I bought). 買いました is the polite form. It doesn’t come before a noun.
items.L22-q19: Before 約束 (plan to meet), 時間 and 用事, use the dictionary form: 見る約束 (பார்க்கும் வாக்கு, a promise to see). 見た would change the meaning to "a promise of having seen". That doesn’t match 明日 (tomorrow).
items.L22-q20: To offer help, "shall I carry it?" = 持ちましょうか (நான் தூக்கட்டுமா?). 持ちましょう would be an invitation: "let’s (both) carry it".
items.L22-q21: 静か is a な-adjective. Before a noun it needs な: 静かな部屋 (அமைதியான அறை, a quiet room). 静かの is wrong. This mistake comes from thinking of Tamil "-ஆன". 静かで is only used to join it to another adjective.
items.L22-q22: あそこで 新聞を 読んでいる 人は 田中さんです。 — (அங்கே செய்தித்தாள் படித்துக்கொண்டிருப்பவர் தனாகா, the person reading a newspaper over there is Tanaka). The describing part (新聞を 読んでいる) comes before the noun 人. 読んでいる goes in the star position.
items.L22-q23: これは 姉が 去年 作った セーターです。 — The describing part is 姉が 去年 作った. The noun セーター comes after it. 作った goes in the star position.
items.L22-q24: 今日は 服を 買う 時間が ありません。 — "To do what" (服を 買う) + 時間が + ありません. 時間が goes in the star position.
items.L22-q25: ［1］ Next comes "but it is cheap". So there must be a bad point before it: 狭い (குறுகலான, small). ［2］ "The room where my friend lives now" = 友達が住んでいる部屋. Use が inside the describing part, and the verb in 〜ている. ［3］ The plan for 日曜日に (Sunday) must end in the polite form, so use 見に行きます. Ending with the short form 行く doesn’t match the polite style of this passage.
